title: Interface and Usability Rules
purpose: Keep user-facing changes clear, usable, accessible, responsive, and consistent with the existing product experience.

rules.statement: Design workflows that reduce cognitive load and make the next action clear.
Make status, progress, errors, empty states, disabled states, loading states, and success states visible and understandable.
Prevent costly accidental actions with confirmation, undo, disabled states, input constraints, or safe defaults.
Preserve user-entered work when validation fails.
Use semantic controls, keyboard-accessible workflows, sufficient contrast, readable text, accessible names, and non-color-only state communication where the platform supports it.
Design layouts that remain usable across expected viewport sizes, device classes, and input methods without overlapping or hidden critical content.
Follow the existing design system, component library, and platform conventions already present in the project.
